subject.title: [Feature]: Pre-reset agentic memory flush — /new and daily reset should get the same memory flush as compaction

question: Should OpenClaw run a silent agentic memory flush before manual and automatic session resets, and if so what default, timeout, provider/privacy, and plugin-boundary contract should own it?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix would add silent tool-capable model execution at a destructive lifecycle boundary and may require new config or plugin API behavior; automation should not choose that security/product boundary.

options.title: Design guarded opt-in contract
options.body: Add reset-time agentic flush only behind an explicit lifecycle contract with timeout, audit/redaction, provider routing, empty-session skips, and regression tests for `/new`, `/reset`, daily, and idle rollover.

options.title: Land hook-only preservation first
options.body: Treat the open daily/idle hook PR as the near-term path and defer agentic flush until after hook dedupe and privacy behavior are proven.

options.title: Keep reset memory plugin-owned
options.body: Require memory plugins or ClawHub packages to own reset persistence unless they can show a missing generic core/plugin API.

recommendation.title: Design guarded opt-in contract
recommendation.body: Add reset-time agentic flush only behind an explicit lifecycle contract with timeout, audit/redaction, provider routing, empty-session skips, and regression tests for `/new`, `/reset`, daily, and idle rollover.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced both the original pre-compaction flush and `/new` reset behavior, making them the best available owner for the cross-boundary product/security decision.
